summary: Randall Degges delivers a brief opening keynote for the World's Fair's first Security Track, framing the current state of AI security around three core obstacles that prevent developers from building and shipping AI-powered software at scale. First, he notes that AI-generated code can contain security vulnerabilities, a well-known issue paralleling human-written code, now treated as a standard part of the development lifecycle through security integration. Second, and more interesting to him, is the challenge of deploying autonomous agents into production environments in a way that allows engineers to sleep without worry, as these agents could go off the rails and harm the business or users. Third, he points to geopolitical disruptions affecting access to frontier models, citing audience frustration when access to a model called Fable was pulled and the inability to use newer models like GPT-5.6. He synthesizes all three obstacles into a single unsolved problem: the need to use AI fearlessly while ensuring it is secure by default. Degges announces that the Security Track will run all day in room 2005 on the second floor, featuring presentations from companies including Nvidia, Anthropic, Keycard, and Snyk. As emcee, he invites attendees to join the sessions aimed at helping them level up their AI development practices without security worries. The talk serves as both a call to action and a roadmap for the day's security-focused content.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Excitement About Generative AI
sections.summary: Randall Degges introduces himself as a lifelong developer and security professional, expressing excitement about how generative AI enables building better quality software more quickly and sparking joy in users.

sections.title: Three Obstacles to AI Development at Scale
sections.summary: Degges identifies three barriers: AI-generated code containing security vulnerabilities, the risk of autonomous agents going off the rails in production, and geopolitical disruptions to frontier model access. He notes the core unsolved problem is using AI fearlessly with security by default.

sections.title: Security Track Announcement
sections.summary: Degges announces the first Security Track at the World's Fair, running all day in room 2005 on the second floor, featuring presenters from Nvidia, Anthropic, Keycard, and Snyk. He will emcee the event all day.
